title: Post-review hardening: correctness, parity, and validation
description:
## Context
A critical review of 2026-02-11 changes found correctness and process gaps that are not fully covered by current CI/test wiring.

## Goal
Restore generator correctness, enforce fixture parity, harden CI validation, and tighten test maintainability/coverage signals.

## Problem Statement
The current branch can pass `cabal test` while `make test` fails due fixture drift, and generator output may be unsound for normal user tables because `oid` is injected beyond system catalogs.

## Default Decisions
- Canonical local/CI validation command is `make test`.
- CI pass criteria apply to PR and protected branch pushes.
- Coverage policy is hard-fail below threshold.
- Coverage threshold target is 100%.
- Coverage scope is `src/**/*.hs` only.
- Generated modules are excluded from coverage scope.
- Exclusions are allowed via explicit, documented allowlist entries (line-level permitted) with rationale.
- `br lint` must stay clean for this epic and descendants.

## Deliverables
- Correct OID handling for generated table columns.
- Canonical generated fixtures committed and enforced.
- CI gate that catches fixture drift before merge.
- Stronger acceptance tests for workflow wiring.
- Usable coverage reporting path in CI with hard-fail policy.
- Reduced test-helper duplication.
- Removal of deprecated test API usage.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] All child tasks are closed with their acceptance tests satisfied.
- [ ] `make test` passes locally in a clean worktree.
- [ ] CI runs pass for PR and protected-branch workflow paths.
- [ ] `br lint` reports no missing required sections for epic + descendants.
- [ ] `br epic status` marks this epic eligible to close.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Generator output for user schemas does not claim non-existent `oid` columns.
- [ ] Fixture parity is enforced by automated checks.
- [ ] CI failures are actionable and aligned with local developer workflow.
- [ ] Coverage gate enforces 100% for `src/**/*.hs`.

title: Fix unsound OID column injection in generated table schemas
description:
## Problem
`squealgen.sql` currently unions an `"oid"` column for all regular tables (`relkind='r'`) in the chosen schema. This is unsound for normal user tables, which do not expose an `oid` column by default.

## Scope
- Restrict synthetic `oid` emission to relations that actually expose an OID system column.
- Keep `pg_catalog` behavior working for catalog tables that do expose `oid` (e.g. `pg_class`).
- Preserve deterministic output ordering.

## Default Decisions
- OID inclusion is metadata-driven, not schema-name-driven.
- OID is emitted only when relation metadata proves the system column exists (e.g. `pg_attribute` evidence for `oid` as a system column).
- Legacy relations that truly expose OID remain supported implicitly through metadata checks.

## Implementation Details
- Replace the current unconditional union in `columnDefs` with attribute-presence checks against catalog metadata.
- Ensure user schemas (e.g. fixtures under `test/Functions`, `test/Checks`, `test/Triggers`) do not receive synthetic `oid` unless truly present.
- Add/adjust regression tests so unsound `oid` insertion cannot regress.

## Validation Plan
- Confirm generated output for a normal table does not contain `"oid"` unless physically present.
- Confirm `PgCatalog` fixture still includes `oid` where expected.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] `squealgen` output for non-catalog fixture tables omits synthetic `"oid"` unless relation metadata proves it exists.
- [ ] `PgCatalog` regression still validates `oid` for catalog relations that expose it.
- [ ] Regression test demonstrates metadata-driven behavior (presence/absence) rather than schema-name heuristics.
- [ ] `cabal test --test-show-details=direct` passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All acceptance tests pass.
- [ ] No remaining unsound `"oid"` claims in generated user-schema fixtures.

title: Regenerate and commit canonical generated test fixtures
description:
## Problem
Generated fixture modules in `test/*/Public.hs` are currently out of sync with generator output, so `make test` fails even when `cabal test` passes.

## Scope
- Regenerate all checked-in generated fixture modules from canonical inputs.
- Commit deterministic fixture updates.
- Verify there is no hidden drift across fixtures.

## Default Decisions
- Canonical fixture generation path is the existing `Makefile`/`buildTestSchema.sh` workflow.
- Determinism proof requires a two-pass run: second run produces zero diff.
- Generated summary blocks (omitted/fallback sections) are treated as canonical output, not manually edited.

## Implementation Details
- Run canonical generation for all fixture schemas.
- Resolve fixture-specific breakages introduced by corrected generator behavior (especially post-OID fix).
- Ensure all generated files are checked in and reproducible.

## Validation Plan
- Run `make test` from a clean state and ensure no mismatch errors from `check_schema`.
- Run fixture generation twice and assert the second pass yields no diffs.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] `make test` completes successfully with no generated-file mismatch failures.
- [ ] Running canonical fixture generation twice results in zero diff on second pass.
- [ ] No manual hand-edits are required after regeneration; committed fixtures are canonical.
- [ ] `cabal test --test-show-details=direct` passes after regeneration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All generated fixture files are in sync with current `squealgen` output.
- [ ] Local developer workflow (`make test`) is green end-to-end.

title: Enforce generated fixture parity in CI
description:
## Problem
CI currently runs `cabal test` and `check_squealgen_drift.sh` but does not enforce full fixture parity via the canonical workflow, allowing drift to merge.

## Scope
- Align CI validation with the canonical local workflow.
- Ensure generated fixture mismatch is a merge blocker.
- Keep CI failures attributable and actionable.

## Default Decisions
- CI uses `make test` as the canonical parity and test gate.
- Keep explicit environment setup for PostgreSQL client tools on Ubuntu runners.
- CI must fail on any generated fixture mismatch.

## Implementation Details
- Update `.github/workflows/ci.yml` so the test gate runs `make test`.
- Preserve or improve failure messaging so drift/parity errors are diagnosable from logs.
- Remove redundant steps only if failure attribution remains clear.

## Validation Plan
- Verify CI-equivalent local command path fails on intentional fixture mismatch.
- Verify clean branch passes the updated command path.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] CI workflow invokes `make test` as the canonical gate.
- [ ] Intentional fixture mismatch produces non-zero failure in CI-equivalent command path.
- [ ] Clean branch passes with no workflow regressions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CI and local developer checks enforce the same canonical parity guarantees.
- [ ] Drift cannot pass CI undetected.

title: Harden workflow acceptance tests with behavioral assertions
description:
## Problem
Existing workflow-wiring tests mostly assert string presence in `Makefile`/CI YAML, which can pass even when behavior is wrong.

## Scope
- Upgrade acceptance tests from static string checks to behavioral assertions.
- Prove mismatch detection and failure propagation in expected command paths.

## Default Decisions
- Behavioral assertions are primary; static substring checks are optional supplemental checks only.
- Tests must run in temporary isolated workspaces and avoid reliance on machine-global state.
- This task validates behavior; task `.3` owns CI workflow implementation.

## Implementation Details
- Extend `CheckSchemaScript.DBSpec` (or equivalent) with behavior-driven checks that execute commands in temp repos/workspaces.
- Add cases for:
  - mismatch detected by canonical workflow path,
  - clean fixture state passing,
  - failure propagation with actionable stderr.
- Retain lightweight static checks only where they add value without being primary guarantees.

## Validation Plan
- Verify tests fail when parity behavior is removed/broken.
- Verify tests pass when wiring is correct.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] At least one behavioral test proves mismatch causes non-zero exit in canonical workflow path.
- [ ] At least one behavioral test proves clean state passes.
- [ ] Behavioral tests (not string-only checks) are sufficient to detect wiring regressions.
- [ ] `cabal test --test-show-details=direct` passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Workflow validation tests fail on real behavioral regressions, not merely on text edits.

title: Add reliable CI coverage reporting and policy
description:
## Problem
There is no reliable, automated coverage signal in CI. Local `--enable-coverage` currently passes tests but fails at HPC report resolution, so coverage cannot be tracked.

## Scope
- Establish a repeatable coverage workflow that runs in CI.
- Fix or work around current HPC path/reporting failures.
- Enforce a hard-fail coverage threshold.

## Default Decisions
- Coverage policy is hard fail below threshold.
- Threshold is 100%.
- Coverage scope is `src/**/*.hs` only.
- Generated modules are excluded from coverage scope.
- Exclusions are allowed via explicit allowlist entries with per-entry rationale.
- Line-level exclusions are permitted when absolutely necessary.
- Coverage output must be visible in CI (artifact and/or summary) on every run.

## Implementation Details
- Resolve Cabal/HPC report generation issues for this project layout.
- Add a dedicated CI job (or CI step) for coverage generation and threshold enforcement.
- Version-control the exclusion allowlist/policy so changes are reviewable.

## Validation Plan
- Coverage command completes without HPC mix/tix resolution errors.
- CI job fails if measured coverage across `src/**/*.hs` drops below 100%.
- Excluded lines/modules are traceable to explicit, justified config.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] `cabal test --enable-coverage` (or equivalent) completes without HPC resolution errors.
- [ ] CI hard-fails when measured coverage for `src/**/*.hs` is <100%.
- [ ] CI passes at 100% measured coverage for `src/**/*.hs`.
- [ ] Generated modules are excluded from measured coverage scope.
- [ ] Exclusion allowlist exists in-repo with documented rationale for each exclusion (including line-level exclusions where used).
- [ ] CI publishes coverage artifact or summary each run.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Team can answer "what changed in coverage" from CI output.
- [ ] 100% threshold is enforced for `src/**/*.hs` coverage scope.

title: Deduplicate generator setup helpers across DB specs
description:
## Problem
Generator-invocation setup logic is duplicated across DBSpec files, increasing maintenance overhead and risk of inconsistent behavior.

## Scope
- Consolidate repeated `runGenerator`/setup patterns into shared helpers.
- Keep existing test semantics intact.

## Default Decisions
- `test/DBHelpers.hs` is the default home for shared generator setup helpers.
- Minimum migration scope includes `Functions.DBSpec`, `Checks.DBSpec`, and `Triggers.DBSpec`.
- Duplication target is zero local duplicated setup helpers in those modules.

## Implementation Details
- Introduce shared helper(s) in `test/DBHelpers.hs` for common generator setup tasks.
- Migrate duplicated setup in targeted suites.
- Preserve fixture-specific assertions while centralizing boilerplate.

## Validation Plan
- Confirm no behavior change by running full suite.
- Confirm targeted specs no longer define duplicated local generator setup helpers.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] Repeated generator setup boilerplate is removed from targeted DBSpec modules.
- [ ] Shared helper API is used by `Functions.DBSpec`, `Checks.DBSpec`, and `Triggers.DBSpec`.
- [ ] Targeted modules contain zero duplicated local `runGenerator`-style setup helpers.
- [ ] `cabal test --test-show-details=direct` passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Duplication reduction is explicit and measurable with no test behavior regressions.

title: Remove deprecated notNull usage in function tests
description:
## Problem
`Functions.DBSpec` uses deprecated `notNull` helpers, generating warnings and increasing future upgrade risk.

## Scope
- Replace deprecated APIs in tests with supported equivalents.
- Keep all test intent and behavior unchanged.

## Default Decisions
- Migration scope is all repository test modules (`test/**/*.hs`), not only one file.
- Deprecated `notNull` usage is removed in favor of supported APIs (`just_` or equivalent).
- Acceptance targets project-module deprecation warnings (not external dependency noise).

## Implementation Details
- Migrate deprecated `notNull` usage across test code.
- Update related expressions/call sites to keep types explicit and readable.
- Ensure no new deprecation warnings are introduced in project test modules.

## Validation Plan
- Run full test suite and confirm behavior remains unchanged.
- Verify deprecation warnings tied to project test modules are eliminated.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] Deprecated `notNull` usage is removed from `test/**/*.hs`.
- [ ] `cabal test --test-show-details=direct` passes after migration.
- [ ] Build/test output contains no deprecation warnings originating from project test modules.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test code uses non-deprecated APIs compatible with current supported Squeal interfaces.

title: Post-review hardening follow-up (coverage, CI, drift, test rigor)
description:
## Context
Strict review of the branch diff against `origin/main` surfaced unresolved reliability and maintainability risks, including:
- Coverage gate passing as `not-applicable` on `0/0` expression coverage (`check_coverage.sh`, `Makefile`, CI workflow wiring).
- A CI failure mode where coverage-enabled builds fail before reporting due to dependency/toolchain constraints.
- Drift check and CI workflow inefficiencies that add unnecessary rebuild/I/O churn.
- Brittle tests that overfit implementation details or rely on heavy mocking for integration behavior.
- Safety and clarity gaps in script guardrails and generated output messaging.

## Goal
Land a coherent hardening pass so `make ci` is meaningful, stable, and measurable.

## Scope
- Coverage gate semantics and fail-closed behavior
- Coverage toolchain compatibility and actionable failure handling
- CI duplication/performance cleanup
- Drift-check regeneration churn reduction
- Test robustness improvements (behavioral > textual/mocked)
- Safety guardrails for destructive paths in scripts
- Documentation/output wording clarity for fallback semantics

## Default Decisions
- CI baseline environment for validation: GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest`, workflow-defined GHC/Cabal versions.
- Epic completion requires all child issues closed (no implicit descoping).
- CI performance target is measured against current failing-run baseline (~9m51s wall clock): improve by at least 15% or 90 seconds, whichever is smaller.
- CI coverage policy on zero-denominator (`expressions_total=0`) is fail-closed; CI must fail until measurable expression scope exists.

## Non-Goals
- Re-architecting `squealgen.sql` generation pipeline
- Expanding schema feature support beyond issues identified in this review

## Success Criteria
- [ ] All child issues are closed.
- [ ] `make test` and `make ci` pass on a clean checkout and in GitHub Actions.
- [ ] Coverage gate behavior is explicit, deterministic, and cannot silently pass as a no-op without an intentional policy declaration.
- [ ] CI runtime is reduced by removing avoidable duplicate work.
- [ ] Script safety and messaging/documentation are aligned with actual behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All child issues are closed.
- [ ] `make test` and `make ci` pass locally and in GitHub Actions PR runs.
- [ ] CI wall clock improvement target (>=15% or >=90s vs ~9m51 baseline) is documented with before/after evidence.
- [ ] Coverage policy outcomes and failure classes are machine-readable and human-readable.
- [ ] CI fails when expression coverage denominator is zero until measurable expression scope exists.

title: Make coverage gate policy meaningful when expression denominator is zero
description:
## Problem
`check_coverage.sh` currently defaults `COVERAGE_ZERO_DENOMINATOR_POLICY=allow`, and `make ci`/CI do not force a strict policy contract. This allows a green coverage gate when expression coverage is `0/0` (`coverage_gate_result=not-applicable`) and can become a silent no-op.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `make ci` in the current repository shape where source modules can produce `0/0` expression coverage.
2. Inspect `coverage/summary.txt`.
3. Observe `expressions_total=0` and `coverage_gate_result=not-applicable` while the coverage step exits success.

## Scope
- Make zero-denominator behavior explicit and fail-closed for CI.
- Preserve a local explicit override only for manual/non-CI workflows if needed.
- Emit unambiguous policy outcome metadata.

## Default Decisions
- Default behavior when `expressions_total=0`: fail (non-zero exit).
- CI must not use an override to pass `0/0`; CI fails until measurable expression scope exists.
- If local override is used manually, output must clearly indicate pass-by-policy (`not-applicable`) instead of measured pass.

## Validation
- Local: run `./check_coverage.sh` with and without override on a `0/0` scope.
- CI-equivalent: validate through `make ci` invocation path and ensure `0/0` fails.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Zero-denominator path fails by default with explicit actionable error.
- [ ] CI configuration does not bypass zero-denominator failure via allow override.
- [ ] `coverage/summary.txt` contains deterministic fields: policy, trigger flag, outcome, gate result.
- [ ] Regression tests cover default-fail path and local manual override path.

title: Fix coverage gate toolchain compatibility in GitHub Actions
description:
## Problem
GitHub Actions currently fails in the coverage step due to toolchain/dependency interactions under `--enable-coverage` before any report is produced. The gate is unstable in real CI.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run the current CI workflow (`Validation contract (CI)` invoking `make ci`).
2. Observe successful `make test` execution.
3. Observe failure in `./check_coverage.sh` during coverage-enabled build phase before report evaluation.

## Scope
- Reproduce and fix coverage command compatibility in CI and local clean environments.
- Adjust invocation strategy (command shape/flags/build targets/workflow wiring) for deterministic behavior.
- Improve diagnostics so failures are actionable.

## Default Decisions
- Validation baseline: GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest` with workflow-pinned GHC/Cabal.
- Success stability requirement: 3 consecutive green CI runs on unchanged commit.
- Failure classes must be distinguishable in logs: build/toolchain failure vs coverage-policy failure.

## Validation
- CI: PR workflow run(s) with clean checkout.
- Local: clean working tree `make ci`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Coverage path succeeds in GitHub Actions baseline environment.
- [ ] Three consecutive CI runs pass without coverage-step toolchain failures.
- [ ] Coverage failures (if induced) are clearly categorized in output/logs.
- [ ] At least one non-mocked test/smoke path exercises the real invocation behavior.
notes:
Implementation complete. Added failing regression test first (c598ac4), then fix commit (e126bd6), then CI toolchain compatibility update (85c44be).

What changed:
- check_coverage.sh now builds coverage with --enable-per-component and keeps failure-class diagnostics (coverage-toolchain vs coverage-policy).
- Coverage harness test enforces per-component flag usage during coverage build.
- GitHub Actions CI pinned cabal-version updated to 3.16.0.0 to avoid cabal 3.10 coverage/per-component incompatibility with vector internal libraries.

Validation:
- Local: cabal test --test-show-details=direct passed; make ci passed.
- CI (same unchanged commit 85c44be39a113610306ca3d6e8c6bc13611f10b6): run 21932241761 attempts 1, 2, and 3 all completed success (consecutive green attempts).

title: Remove duplicate build/test work from CI validation contract
description:
## Problem
Current CI path duplicates heavy work: explicit build, test run, then another coverage-enabled build/test cycle. This increases runtime, flake risk, and resource waste.

## Scope
- Remove avoidable duplicate compile/test work across workflow, `Makefile`, and coverage orchestration.
- Keep one canonical validation contract (`make ci`) while preserving drift checks and coverage semantics.

## Default Decisions
- Keep `make ci` as canonical entrypoint.
- Remove standalone workflow steps that duplicate work already performed by `make ci`.
- Performance baseline is the median wall-clock duration of 3 comparable CI runs.
- Performance target for this task: at least 15% or 90s wall-clock improvement vs that median baseline.

## Validation
- CI before/after timing capture (3 comparable runs each side).
- Local sanity: `make ci` still passes and preserves validation ordering.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CI no longer performs redundant full build/test cycles outside canonical contract.
- [ ] `make ci` remains canonical and documented.
- [ ] Median CI runtime improves by target threshold.
- [ ] Documentation reflects final execution order.
notes: Blocked on CI timing evidence for acceptance criterion: GitHub Actions currently has no run for post-change commit 891361e (latest ci.yml runs are for 85c44be, e126bd6, 66d3517, a6ab3d9). Attempted: queried recent CI runs via gh run list and re-validated local make ci pass. Needed next: push commit 891361e and collect 3 comparable post-change CI run durations (and 3 baseline pre-change durations) or explicitly waive the timing threshold criterion.

comments.text: Correction: prior comment included accidental shell-expanded output; ignore that payload. Action needed: please provide 3 comparable baseline CI run times/links and 3 post-change run times/links for this workflow, or confirm we should waive/adjust the median runtime acceptance criterion so this task can be closed.

title: Reduce drift-check regeneration churn on clean runs
description:
## Problem
`check_squealgen_drift.sh` always regenerates `squealgen`, causing avoidable rewrites and downstream rebuild churn even on clean states.

## Scope
- Rework drift detection to minimize mutation on clean paths.
- Preserve correctness in git and non-git modes.
- Keep clear remediation output when drift is detected.

## Default Decisions
- Clean-run non-mutation is validated by unchanged content hash and unchanged file mtime.
- Applies to both git mode and non-git fallback mode when no drift exists.
- Bootstrap behavior when `squealgen` is absent in non-git mode remains supported.

## Validation
- Script-level tests for git mode, non-git mode, mode-bit/content drift, and bootstrap case.
- Local sanity via `make test`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Clean drift checks do not rewrite `squealgen` (content + mtime stable).
- [ ] Drift detection remains correct for content and executable-bit changes.
- [ ] Git and non-git modes remain covered by regression tests.
- [ ] `make test` avoids unnecessary regeneration-induced churn.

title: Replace brittle/mocked contract tests with behavior-focused integration checks
description:
## Problem
Several tests assert source-text implementation details or rely on mocked command shims for core integration behavior, reducing confidence in real-world correctness.

## Scope
- Replace brittle source-text checks with behavior-focused assertions where feasible.
- Add at least one real-tool integration path for coverage command behavior.
- Keep fast unit checks where useful, but avoid over-mocking critical contracts.

## Default Decisions
- Priority replacements include:
  - string-ban style property harness guard tests
  - purely mocked coverage command contract checks for critical CI behavior
- Integration path runs in regular CI (not nightly-only), with bounded runtime impact.
- Runtime budget is incremental: added/modified tests in this task may increase total suite runtime by at most 30s versus pre-task baseline.

## Validation
- Full test suite on clean checkout.
- CI run confirms integration path executes and remains stable.
- Runtime delta is measured against pre-task baseline.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Identified brittle source-text assertions are replaced or justified with behavior-based alternatives.
- [ ] Coverage tests include at least one non-mocked integration invocation path.
- [ ] Test suite remains deterministic and runtime increase stays within incremental budget.
- [ ] Test names/descriptions state behavioral contract clearly.

title: Add guardrails for destructive coverage report directory cleanup
description:
## Problem
`check_coverage.sh` accepts `COVERAGE_REPORT_DIR` and performs destructive cleanup. Unsafe values can target unintended paths.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Set `COVERAGE_REPORT_DIR` to a dangerous path (e.g., `/`, empty, or path escaping workspace).
2. Run `./check_coverage.sh`.
3. Observe cleanup attempts without strict path safety guarantees.

## Scope
- Add strict path safety checks before any destructive cleanup.
- Keep expected behavior for safe in-repo report directories.

## Default Decisions
- Allowed `COVERAGE_REPORT_DIR`: repository-relative subpath under workspace.
- Rejected: empty, `/`, `.`, `..`, absolute paths, and paths that resolve outside workspace (including symlink escapes).
- No unsafe override flag for destructive cleanup in this task.

## Validation
- Unit/script tests for accepted safe path and rejected dangerous paths.
- Manual sanity run with default `coverage/`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dangerous `COVERAGE_REPORT_DIR` values are rejected with clear error messages.
- [ ] Cleanup executes only after path safety validation passes.
- [ ] Symlink/path traversal escapes are rejected.
- [ ] Regression tests cover at least one accepted safe path and multiple rejected unsafe paths.

title: Clarify fallback terminology in generated output and README
description:
## Problem
Generated output labels check constraints as both emitted and "Omitted/fallback" in ways that are easy to misread. README/docs must align with final behavior after coverage/CI/safety changes.

## Scope
- Clarify generated section naming and wording for check-constraint fallback semantics.
- Align README and validation-contract notes with final CI/coverage behavior.
- Update affected fixture expectations.

## Default Decisions
- Docs in scope: README + generated output wording + relevant golden fixture/module expectations.
- This task runs after coverage-policy/toolchain/CI-contract/safety changes are settled.
- No separate changelog entry required in this task unless user requests it later.

## Validation
- Diff review of generated output wording and README consistency.
- Full tests passing with updated fixture expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Generated output terminology unambiguously distinguishes represented constraints vs fallback notes.
- [ ] README matches final validation contract and policy behavior.
- [ ] Relevant fixture expectations are updated and passing.

title: Establish measurable expression coverage scope for strict CI policy
description:
## Problem
CI is now required to fail when coverage expression denominator is zero, but the current `src/**` coverage scope can legitimately produce `0/0` (e.g., type-only modules). Without measurable scope, the epic cannot satisfy both strict policy and green CI.

## Scope
- Ensure coverage scope used by CI contains measurable executable expressions.
- Preserve strict fail-closed zero-denominator policy in CI.
- Keep scope changes minimal and intentional.

## Default Decisions
- CI success requires measurable expression scope (`expressions_total > 0`).
- Do not relax policy to allow `0/0` in CI.
- Prefer small, explicit source/test adjustments over broad scope expansion.

## Validation
- Run `make ci` and verify coverage summary shows `expressions_total > 0`.
- Verify CI remains fail-closed for genuinely non-measurable configurations.
- Confirm test suite still passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `coverage/summary.txt` in CI-equivalent path reports `expressions_total > 0`.
- [ ] `make ci` can pass without using zero-denominator allow override.
- [ ] No policy regression: if scope reverts to non-measurable, CI fails as designed.
- [ ] Changes are documented where coverage scope/policy is described.

title: Post-mainline hardening and reliability fixes
description:
## Context
The repository default branch is now `main`, but the hardening branch review surfaced several concrete reliability and maintainability gaps that should be addressed in a structured follow-up.

## Goal
Close the highest-risk correctness and developer-experience gaps without introducing behavior regressions.

## Scope
- Coverage gate determinism and policy clarity
- Function signature label correctness
- Drift-check/bootstrap ergonomics
- Test robustness and documentation accuracy

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All child issues under this epic are closed.
- [ ] `make test` and `make ci` pass on a clean checkout from `main`.
- [ ] Coverage policy behavior is deterministic and documented.
- [ ] No known overloaded-function label collisions remain for representable signatures.
- [ ] README and workflow docs reflect current behavior.
close_reason: All child issues closed; acceptance verified via commit 0af0f1b and passing clean-checkout gates (make test, make ci).

title: Make coverage gate deterministic for zero-denominator projects
description:
## Problem
`check_coverage.sh` currently fails when expression denominator is `0/0`, which happens in this repository shape (e.g. source modules with only type aliases).

## Desired Outcome
Coverage enforcement should remain strict where meaningful, but deterministic and actionable when denominator is zero.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A documented zero-denominator policy is implemented (for example: explicit N/A mode or configurable behavior).
- [ ] On a clean checkout of `main`, `./check_coverage.sh` no longer fails due solely to `(0/0)` when no executable expressions exist.
- [ ] The report summary includes machine-readable policy outcome metadata.
- [ ] Regression tests cover the zero-denominator path and policy output.

title: Validate COVERAGE_THRESHOLD input as numeric
description:
## Problem
`COVERAGE_THRESHOLD` accepts arbitrary text today; non-numeric values can silently degrade policy enforcement.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `check_coverage.sh` rejects non-numeric threshold values with a clear error and non-zero exit.
- [ ] Numeric values (integer and decimal if supported) continue to work.
- [ ] Tests cover valid and invalid threshold inputs.
close_reason: Completed in commit 0af0f1b with passing validation (cabal test, make test, make ci incl. clean-checkout verification).

title: Fix overloaded-function label collisions across schemas
description:
## Problem
Function disambiguation currently tokenizes argument labels from `typname` only. Different schemas can share the same type name, producing duplicate labels for distinct overloads.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Label generation is collision-resistant for representable overloads that differ by schema-qualified arg types.
- [ ] Generated labels remain deterministic and stable.
- [ ] Compatibility alias behavior remains correct (emit alias only when unambiguous).
- [ ] Add a regression test using same-named arg types from different schemas.
close_reason: Completed in commit 0af0f1b with passing validation (cabal test, make test, make ci incl. clean-checkout verification).

title: Allow first-run drift checks outside git worktrees
description:
## Problem
`make test` invokes drift check before generation, and non-git mode requires an existing `./squealgen`. Fresh non-git bootstraps can fail before initial generation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Fresh non-git checkouts can run local validation without manual pre-seeding of `./squealgen`.
- [ ] Drift detection still fails when generated output actually diverges.
- [ ] Tests cover first-run fallback behavior and drift behavior.
close_reason: Completed in commit 0af0f1b with passing validation (cabal test, make test, make ci incl. clean-checkout verification).

title: Replace brittle source-text assertions with behavior-focused tests
description:
## Problem
Some tests validate source strings in test files rather than runtime behavior, which is easy to bypass and fragile under refactors.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Source-introspection assertions are replaced (or reduced) in favor of behavior-level checks.
- [ ] New tests fail on real regressions and are insensitive to harmless textual refactors.
- [ ] Test runtime remains reasonable.
close_reason: Completed in commit 0af0f1b with passing validation (cabal test, make test, make ci incl. clean-checkout verification).

title: Align README roadmap with implemented features
description:
## Problem
README still lists features as future work that are already implemented (e.g. IN/OUT support, triggers), causing contributor confusion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] README roadmap entries reflect current generator capabilities.
- [ ] Validation contract and branch naming references are consistent with `main`.
- [ ] Documentation changes are reviewed for accuracy against current test coverage.
close_reason: Completed in commit 0af0f1b with passing validation (cabal test, make test, make ci incl. clean-checkout verification).

title: Strict hardening follow-up from prickly review
description:
## Context
A strict review of `review/hardening-stack-2026-02-11` against `origin/master` identified concrete quality gaps despite green core tests.

## Goal
Eliminate coverage false-greens, reduce CI/local mismatch, harden compatibility/documentation guarantees, and remove brittle test/script behavior.

## Findings Addressed
- Coverage gate false-green (0/0 denominator).
- Coverage gate fails on stale `.tix` state.
- Backward-compatibility break in overloaded function naming is undocumented.
- CI and local validation contract mismatch.
- Coverage allowlist does not implement line-level exclusions.
- Workflow tests rely on brittle string checks/tool-specific assumptions.
- Drift check hard-requires git worktree (non-git envs fail).
- Property test harness still uses global `unsafePerformIO` state.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] Each child task has passing acceptance tests and is closed.
- [ ] `make test` passes in a clean repo checkout.
- [ ] Coverage gate behavior is deterministic across repeated runs.
- [ ] CI and local validation contracts are documented and consistent.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] No known false-green coverage path remains.
- [ ] Backward-compat behavior for function naming is explicit and tested.
- [ ] Script/test brittleness and environment assumptions are reduced.

title: Fix coverage false-green when denominator is zero
description:
## Problem
`check_coverage.sh` can pass with `100% (0/0)` expressions, which is a false green and invalidates the gate.

## Scope
- Reject zero-denominator coverage results.
- Ensure coverage parsing captures numerator/denominator, not percentage alone.

## Implementation Details
- Parse `hpc report` expression line for numerator and denominator.
- Fail when denominator is zero for in-scope measured modules.
- Emit clear diagnostics including parsed counts.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] Gate fails when expression denominator is `0`.
- [ ] Gate passes only when denominator is `>0` and percentage meets threshold.
- [ ] `check_coverage.sh` output includes parsed numerator/denominator.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No `100% (0/0)` run can pass the coverage gate.

title: Make coverage gate robust to stale tix/mix state
description:
## Problem
Coverage runs can fail nondeterministically due stale or hash-mismatched `.tix` artifacts.

## Scope
- Make coverage runs repeatable in the same workspace.
- Avoid stale `.tix`/mix collisions.

## Implementation Details
- Ensure report dir `.tix` is cleaned/recreated per run (or use unique tix path).
- Validate/refresh mix directory inputs before `hpc report`.
- Keep failure messages explicit when hash mismatch occurs.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] Running `check_coverage.sh` twice consecutively in same workspace succeeds deterministically.
- [ ] No stale `.tix` hash mismatch failure after first successful run.
- [ ] CI coverage step is stable across reruns/retries.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Coverage gate is idempotent under repeated execution.

title: Recover and document backward compatibility for overloaded function names
description:
## Problem
Overloaded function disambiguation (`name__argtokens`) changes generated symbols and can break downstream code. Migration path is unclear.

## Scope
- Recover backward compatibility with aliases where unambiguous.
- Keep deterministic disambiguated labels for overloaded signatures.
- Document/annotate cases where compatibility aliases cannot be emitted.

## Default Decisions
- Always emit disambiguated labels for overloaded signatures.
- Emit compatibility alias using the legacy simple name (`name`) only when exactly one representable signature exists for that base name after filtering.
- Do not emit legacy alias when two or more representable signatures remain (ambiguous).
- When alias cannot be emitted, include explicit generated notes explaining why.
- Treat ambiguous/non-representable overloaded groups as not having had a sensible stable interface previously.

## Implementation Details
- Add alias-emission logic at function classification/output stage.
- Ensure alias entries do not introduce duplicate key conflicts in generated Squeal function maps.
- Add migration notes in README/changelog documenting alias behavior and ambiguity limits.
- Add deterministic tests for:
  - single representable overload among filtered signatures -> alias emitted,
  - multiple representable overloads -> no alias + explanatory note,
  - non-overloaded functions unchanged.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] Legacy alias is emitted when overload group is unambiguous after representability filtering.
- [ ] No alias is emitted for ambiguous overload groups; explanatory note is present.
- [ ] Existing non-overloaded names remain unchanged.
- [ ] Generated output remains deterministic and compiles.
- [ ] README/changelog includes migration guidance and aliasing limitations.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Backward compatibility is recovered where technically safe and unambiguous.
- [ ] Ambiguous cases are explicitly documented in generated output and project docs.
close_reason: Completed: added deterministic overload compatibility aliases, ambiguity notes, migration docs, and validated via full test suite

title: Unify and document local vs CI validation contract
description:
## Problem
Local canonical check (`make test`) and CI checks are inconsistent, creating avoidable local/CI mismatch risk.

## Scope
- Define a single validation contract and enforce/document it.
- Ensure developers can run the same gates locally that CI enforces.

## Implementation Details
- Decide whether coverage gate belongs in `make test`, dedicated `make ci`, or documented split contract.
- Update Makefile and README to reflect contract.
- Ensure failure messages indicate which contract path failed.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] Validation contract (local vs CI) is explicitly documented.
- [ ] Make targets mirror CI-required gates (or clearly define approved split).
- [ ] At least one automated test verifies contract wiring behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Local and CI expectations are consistent and predictable.

title: Add line-level coverage exclusion support
description:
## Problem
Coverage allowlist supports only module-level exclusions, not line-level entries despite policy direction.

## Scope
- Implement line-level exclusion support in coverage policy tooling.
- Keep policy auditable with rationale per exclusion.

## Implementation Details
- Extend allowlist format to include line-level selectors (e.g. `Module.Name:line` or range form).
- Validate format and rationale for each entry.
- Ensure module-level and line-level exclusions can coexist without ambiguity.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] Line-level exclusion entries are parsed and enforced.
- [ ] Malformed allowlist entries fail with actionable errors.
- [ ] Each exclusion entry requires a rationale.
- [ ] Coverage report output includes applied exclusions summary.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Coverage exclusions support audited line-level precision.
close_reason: Completed: line-level coverage exclusions implemented with selector/rationale validation, applied-exclusion summary, and passing targeted/full tests

title: Harden workflow tests by removing brittle string/exit-code checks
description:
## Problem
Workflow tests still rely on brittle text checks and tool-specific exit-code assumptions.

## Scope
- Replace brittle assertions with behavior-based checks.
- Reduce portability assumptions across `make` variants/environments.

## Implementation Details
- Prefer command outcome and stderr/behavior assertions over substring checks in config files.
- Avoid asserting specific make implementation exit code values when semantics can be asserted directly.
- Keep minimal static checks only when behavior cannot be simulated.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] Workflow tests fail for real behavioral regressions and pass for harmless formatting changes.
- [ ] Tests no longer depend on exact `make` exit code numerics unless strictly required.
- [ ] Full suite passes across supported dev/CI environments.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Workflow tests are behavior-first and less brittle.
close_reason: Completed: replaced make-specific exit-code assertion with behavior-based check and validated with full cabal test suite

title: Add explicit non-git fallback behavior for squealgen drift checking
description:
## Problem
`check_squealgen_drift.sh` hard-fails outside a git worktree, which blocks some non-git packaging/source environments.

## Scope
- Make drift checking behavior explicit for git and non-git contexts.
- Preserve strong drift guarantees in normal development/CI usage.

## Implementation Details
- Add explicit mode selection (strict git mode vs non-git fallback).
- In non-git mode, compare regenerated `squealgen` content against committed file checksum/content when possible.
- Document expected behavior and limitations.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] Drift check behaves correctly in git worktree mode (existing guarantees preserved).
- [ ] Drift check has a documented non-git path with deterministic behavior.
- [ ] CI remains strict and unchanged in safety guarantees.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Drift tooling no longer fails ambiguously in non-git environments.
close_reason: Completed: added explicit drift modes with deterministic non-git fallback, documented behavior, and verified by targeted + full test suite

title: Refactor Property.DDLSpec to remove unsafe global execution state
description:
## Problem
`Property/DDLSpec` still relies on `unsafePerformIO` and global mutable refs for execution checks, which is brittle and hard to reason about.

## Scope
- Remove global mutable/unsafe state from property execution tracking.
- Keep all current property intent and validation.

## Implementation Details
- Refactor execution bookkeeping to explicit state threading or framework-supported hooks.
- Eliminate `unsafePerformIO` for test-control state where feasible.
- Preserve determinism and readable failure messages.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] Property suite no longer uses global `unsafePerformIO` refs for execution tracking.
- [ ] Existing property assertions still run and fail/pass as intended.
- [ ] `cabal test --test-show-details=direct` passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Property harness is less hacky and easier to maintain.
close_reason: Completed: removed global unsafe execution refs from Property.DDLSpec and validated with full cabal test suite

title: Squealgen generator hardening and feature completion
description:
## Context
A repository audit on 2026-02-11 identified correctness risks, workflow drift, duplication, and shallow coverage in `squealgen`.

## Goal
Ship a reliability/coverage hardening pass and close the known feature gaps called out in code comments and `README.md`.

## Deliverables
- Generator correctness fixes
- Workflow and drift-detection hardening
- Test coverage upgrades (especially current compile-only tests)
- Missing feature implementations (functions/checks/triggers)

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] `br epic status` shows this epic at 100% and eligible to close.
- [ ] `cabal test --test-show-details=direct` passes on the pinned toolchain.
- [ ] `br lint` reports no missing required sections for epic + child tasks.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] All child tasks are closed.
- [ ] Full test suite passes: cabal test --test-show-details=direct.
- [ ] Epic is eligible for closure in br epic status.

title: Enforce squealgen.sql/squealgen drift checks in CI and local workflow
description:
## Problem
`squealgen.sql` and generated `squealgen` can drift, causing local behavior/CI behavior mismatches.

## Scope
- Add an explicit drift check that regenerates `squealgen` and fails if `git diff` is non-empty.
- Wire the check into CI and local test workflow.
- Document the source-of-truth policy.

## Default Decisions
- Drift check validates both file content and executable mode for `squealgen`.
- Drift check runs in CI and is invoked from local `make test`.
- Failure output includes a single remediation command: `./mksquealgen.sh`.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] If `squealgen.sql` is edited without regenerating `squealgen`, drift check fails non-zero.
- [ ] If `squealgen` executable mode drifts, drift check fails non-zero.
- [ ] Running `./mksquealgen.sh` then drift check passes.
- [ ] CI runs drift check and fails on drift.
- [ ] `make test` executes drift check before/with test execution.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Make check_schema fail fast on generated-file mismatches
description:
## Problem
`check_schema` prints mismatch warnings but does not fail (`exit 1` is disabled), allowing stale generated test modules.

## Scope
- Make mismatch a hard failure in `check_schema`.
- Keep output actionable (show diff and clear failure message).
- Verify `buildTestSchema.sh` propagates the failure.

## Default Decisions
- On mismatch, `check_schema` exits non-zero and does not copy over the target file.
- No implicit overwrite path; regeneration remains explicit.

## Acceptance Tests
- [ ] Intentional mismatch causes `check_schema` to exit non-zero.
- [ ] Matching files produce zero exit.
- [ ] `buildTestSchema.sh` propagates failures correctly.
- [ ] `make test` still passes when generated files are current.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All items under "## Acceptance Tests" are satisfied.
- [ ] `cabal test --test-show-details=direct` passes after implementation.
notes: Current blocker (2026-02-11): After implementing check_schema fail-fast and pg_tmp compatibility (wal_keep_size), make test no longer fails at Postgres startup. It now fails due generated file drift, as intended by check_schema. Attempted to regenerate all test/*/Public.hs in a clean worktree; regeneration succeeded, but subsequent compile fails with schema/type drift (unexpected oid/default metadata in generated user-table columns), causing multiple DBSpec type errors (ComplexPrimary, Domains, Members, etc.). What is needed next: decide whether to (a) scope/fix generator drift in this task so regenerated schemas compile and make test passes, or (b) treat this as separate upstream task and relax/adjust this task acceptance accordingly.
